title: Stable pointed moduli groupoids and abelian level structures
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $g\geq2$, $r\geq0$ be integers. A stable ordered $r$-pointed genus-$g$ curve over an $S$-scheme $T$ is a stable pointed curve $(f:X\to T,s_1,\ldots,s_r)$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve], with labelled sections and projectivity in the projective-bundle convention [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], such that for every geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point] its geometric fibre $X_{\bar t}=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product] has arithmetic genus $\dim_\Omega H^1(X_{\bar t},\mathcal O_{X_{\bar t}})=g$. Here $\Omega$ is an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and this is Zariski cohomology of the structure sheaf [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]. The family is smooth when $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

Write $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,r}(T)$ for the groupoid of these families, with arrows the $T$-isomorphisms $\alpha:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ such that $\alpha\circ s_i=t_i$ for every label $i$. A groupoid is a category in which every arrow is invertible. The total category $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,r}$ lies over $\mathit{Sch}/S$: an arrow over $u:T'\to T$ from $(X'/T',s'_i)$ to $(X/T,s_i)$ is an isomorphism $X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X\times_TT'$ over $T'$ preserving all the pulled-back sections. Composition uses the canonical associativity isomorphism of scheme fibre products. Pullback along $u$ is the family $X\times_TT'\to T'$ with sections $t'\mapsto(s_i(u(t')),t')$. The category $\mathcal M_{g,r}$ is its full subcategory of smooth families. A category $p:\mathcal F\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ is fibred in groupoids when every base arrow $u:T'\to T$ and object $x$ over $T$ has a lift $y\to x$ over $u$, and whenever $a:y\to x$, $b:z\to x$ and $v:p(z)\to p(y)$ satisfy $p(a)v=p(b)$ there is a unique $c:z\to y$ over $v$ with $ac=b$. Morphisms between such categories are functors over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, and 2-morphisms are natural isomorphisms over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. A map from $T$ to a moduli groupoid means an object over $T$, and a 2-isomorphism between such maps means an isomorphism of those objects. We retain families and their automorphisms, rather than replacing a fibre groupoid by its set of isomorphism classes.

For functors $F:A\to C$, $G:B\to C$ of groupoids, the 2-fibre product has objects $(a,b,\phi)$ with $\phi:F(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(b)$ and arrows $(a,b,\phi)\to(a',b',\phi')$ given by $(v:a\to a',w:b\to b')$ satisfying $G(w)\phi=\phi'F(v)$. For categories fibred in groupoids this construction is made in each fibre, with the induced pullbacks.

Let $\ell\geq3$ be prime and invertible on $S$, meaning that its image is a unit in every local ring of $S$, and put $A=\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$. For a smooth genus-$g$ family $f:X\to T$ put $\mathcal H_{X/T}=R^1f_*\underline A_X$, using the higher direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Equivalently it is the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $T'\mapsto H^1((X\times_TT')_{\mathrm{et}},\underline A)$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, with restrictions the cohomology pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]; the comparison is [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf]. An abelian level-$\ell$ structure is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\underline A_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] $\lambda:\underline{A^{2g}}_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H_{X/T}$. No symplectic condition is imposed. Let $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}(T)$ have objects the unpointed smooth families together with such a $\lambda$. An arrow $(X,\lambda_X)\to(Y,\lambda_Y)$ is a $T$-isomorphism $\alpha:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ with $\alpha^*\lambda_Y=\lambda_X$. Along $u:T'\to T$, the pulled-back frame is the composite $\underline{A^{2g}}_{T'}\cong u^{-1}\underline{A^{2g}}_T\xrightarrow{u^{-1}\lambda}u^{-1}\mathcal H_{X/T}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}^1}\mathcal H_{X\times_TT'/T'}$, where inverse image is [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], the constant-module comparison is [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module], and $\mathrm{BC}^1$ is degree-one proper base change [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] for the constant torsion sheaf; properness follows from the projective-bundle hypothesis by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper]. These fibre groupoids and pullbacks specify $\mathcal L_{g,\ell}$.

For an $S$-scheme $Q$, let $h_Q(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,Q)$, with precomposition as restriction, regarded as a groupoid with only identity arrows. A scheme represents a moduli groupoid $\mathcal F$ if $h_Q$ and $\mathcal F$ are equivalent over $\mathit{Sch}/S$; in particular the automorphism groups of $\mathcal F(T)$ must then be trivial. Algebraic spaces and maps between them are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A coarse moduli scheme for $\mathcal F$ is an $S$-scheme $Q$ and a map $\pi:\mathcal F\to h_Q$ such that for every algebraic space $Z/S$, composition with $\pi$ gives a bijection between $S$-maps $Q\to Z$ and maps $\mathcal F\to Z$, and for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ it gives a bijection from isomorphism classes in $\mathcal F(\Omega)$ to $Q(\Omega)$. A stack here is a category fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes for which the isomorphisms between any two objects form a sheaf for etale coverings, and every etale descent datum for objects is effective: objects on a cover, with overlap isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle condition, arise by pullback from an object on the base. A Deligne--Mumford stack is such a stack whose diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces and which has a surjective etale scheme atlas. Representable by algebraic spaces means that every 2-base change by a scheme is equivalent to an algebraic space, regarded as a discrete fibred groupoid; etaleness and surjectivity of an atlas are tested after these base changes, using [def-weil-etale-morphism] on scheme charts. These definitions assert no existence of coarse moduli schemes, scheme representatives, or atlases for the moduli groupoids just specified.

proof.text: For StablePointedModuli.pullback_properties, apply isStablePointedCurve_baseChange to the given labelled stable family. This establishes the stability conjunct without imposing or using a prescribed total genus.

For a geometric point b of the new base, use Mathlib pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso to compare the iterated geometric fibre with the original geometric fibre at b followed by a.left. Its hom_snd equation says that this is an isomorphism over the same algebraically closed field. Apply finrank_structureSheafCohomology_iso to its degree-one structure-sheaf cohomology.

Compose the numerical cohomology equality with X.genus at b followed by a.left. Pair this result with the stability conjunct. All existing object, arrow, framing, and stack definitions are unchanged; AbelianLevelModuli.hom_operations retains its existing identity-and-composition proof obligation.

proof_origin.note: Formal reduction of pullback_properties: stability under base change remains one strictly smaller generic theorem; geometric arithmetic genus transport is proved using the canonical iterated-pullback isomorphism and the proved structure-sheaf cohomology dimension comparison. Other definitions and signatures are unchanged.
